name: Cipla Ltd
title: Cipla Ltd - 500087 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Cipla guides FY27 EBITDA margin 18.5-20% and a US$1bn run-rate by FY27 end, excluding Lanreotide; supply-side signals are limited to capex plateauing after 'built enough capacity', with a war-driven cost headwind flagged.

summary.headline: Cipla Q4 FY26 revenue INR 6,541 crore; FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 18.5%-20% excluding Lanreotide, with US $1 billion run-rate target by FY27 end.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 One India grew 15% YoY, with full-year India growth at 9%, and FY26 total revenue of INR 28,163 crore. Quarterly EBITDA margin was 15.2% (21% for the year, excluding other income), and quarterly PAT was INR 555 crore (8.5% of sales). North America reported quarterly revenue of USD 155 million and annual revenue of USD 780 million, with the generic Ventolin AB-rated approval from the US facility as the key milestone. Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin of 18.5%-20%, weighted to H2, and a US run-rate of USD 1 billion by end-FY27, both excluding Lanreotide.

segments.name: One India
segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 15% YoY with double-digit growth in branded prescription, trade generics and consumer health; FY26 growth 9%. Foracort crossed INR 1,000 crore and Dytor reached INR 650 crore (+25%); 33 brands now above INR 100 crore.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue USD 155 million and FY26 USD 780 million; Albuterol share 19.6% (IQVIA MAT March 2026). Generic Ventolin (with CGT) approved, first commercial MDI from US facility, launch expected in coming months.

segments.name: One Africa
segments.commentary: Q4 growth 14% YoY; FY26 growth 7% in USD terms. Private secondary growth 6.6% vs market 4.8%.

segments.name: EMEU
segments.commentary: Scaled to over USD 400 million revenue despite geopolitical volatility from the war; margin stability maintained.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 18.5%-20%, with sequential improvement each quarter and bigger gains in H2; guidance excludes any Lanreotide contribution.
North America targeted to reach USD 1 billion run-rate by end-FY27; this is a run-rate target, not FY27 revenue guidance.
R&D to remain about 6%-7% of revenue, biased towards 7%.
Gross margin expected to have a positive bias, helped by chronic mix (5%-10% better gross margin) and in-house respiratory launches, partly offset by partnered peptide royalties.
Respiratory: four US approvals expected in FY27 (Advair, Symbicort and one other in H1/H2), with 4 of 5 filed assets targeted for commercialisation in FY27.
Lanreotide: partner remediation ongoing; closer visibility expected next quarter; alternate US-based site targeting filing by early calendar 2027 or Q4 FY27.
Capex cycle expected to reduce after about another year; capital to shift to R&D, biosimilars and productivity.
capex_capacity: US facility now supplies generic Ventolin; Goa and two US facilities support launch of four respiratory assets planned for FY27.
Indore site derisked; US and Goa used for filings. Goa recently inspected with two observations responded to, classification awaited.
FDA inspections at Bommasandra, Sitec (Mumbai) and Medispray (Goa) all resulted in VAI or NAI classification during the year.
Biosimilars: 2 in-house assets (one under US IND clinical study); plan to add 1-2 assets per year via Kemwell JV, targeting 6-8 in-house assets over 5-8 years.
Capex increased steadily over the last 3 years; management says cycle should reduce after about a year as capacity is built.
demand_pricing: Ventolin generic: exclusivity of about 6 months under CGT; ramp-up expected in H2 FY27, with supply and device not seen as constraints.
Albuterol share guided at 19.5%-20% of the market; Q3 reading of 22% was not seen as a trend.
US pipeline of 40-50 products to be filed over 3 years, including 12 first-to-files and 8 B2 opportunities; 8 peptide and complex assets already filed with launches between FY27 and FY28.
Management expects a few FY27 US launches with USD 100 million-plus annualised potential, plus other large and medium opportunities; tail expected to taper gradually rather than cliff.
India Q4 benefit from Pfizer in-licensed brands and Inzpera acquisition; Q4 secondary growth improved in April over March.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any shelf stock adjustment for Revlimid in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: No SSA adjustments were booked in the quarter, consistent with the prior quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to US USD 1 billion, and how much is contributed by new products?
qa_highlights.answer: The USD 1 billion is a run-rate target by end-FY27, not FY27 revenue, and depends on pipeline approvals (Ventolin already approved, plus Advair, Symbicort, one other respiratory, a big peptide and three smaller assets). Lanreotide is excluded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Lanreotide?
qa_highlights.answer: The partner is remediating and a reinspection is expected; visibility expected by next quarter. An alternate US site targets filing by early calendar 2027 or Q4 FY27, with return targeted from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin guidance 18.5%-20% and is it conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investment in people and R&D is continuing; the investment phase is ending. H1 is expected to be lower margin and H2 better than average. Management said 20%-plus should be sustainable beyond FY27, and the guide assumes temporary war-related cost pressure.

qa_highlights.question: How is gross margin expected to evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin is expected to have a positive bias: in-house respiratory products and chronic mix (5%-10% better gross margin) help, while partnered peptide royalties dilute. War-related sourcing costs are a temporary headwind.

qa_highlights.question: Can India outpace market growth in FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects strong double-digit growth and market-beating performance in FY27-28, citing consistent trend over the last couple of quarters after a muted Q1 FY26 in branded Rx.

risks_watch: Lanreotide remediation and FDA reinspection timing; no revenue included in guidance.
War-related sourcing and input cost pressure, which management says will hit inventory costs in H2 and is not yet quantified if it persists.
Respiratory approval timing (Advair, Symbicort, others) and launch timing; a 1-2 month slip changes full-year revenue.
Indore site classification and Goa observations pending FDA classification.
Price erosion as competition enters the newly launched products; management says tail will taper gradually.
Rising R&D spend (INR 509 crore in Q4) and employee cost growth of about 10% YoY versus the FY27 margin target.
summary.management_tone: Confident on US pipeline and India growth, but cautious on near-term margins, citing war-related costs and Lanreotide, which is excluded from guidance. Several answers were hedged on timing of approvals and launches.
key_quotes: We are expecting to launch this product within the coming months.
So the guidance, I just wanted to clarify is a $1 billion run rate by the end of the year.
So therefore, I think 18.5% to 20% is a fair margin to assume.
To be fair, I think it should 20 plus is something that we should anyway sustain going forward.

adds.what: US facility now supplying generic Ventolin (first commercial MDI from US facility)
Goa and two US facilities supporting launch of four respiratory assets planned for FY27

growth.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 18.5%-20% (new) and US run-rate of $1bn by FY27 end (excluding Lanreotide), backed partly by generic Ventolin launch with 6-month exclusivity, four respiratory approvals expected in FY27, and a few $100m+ US launches; no quantified capacity additions or revenue growth guide given, and capex cycle is expected to ease after about a year.
